clue.text: James Lane Allen's invisible singers

parts.note: points to the title of the American novelist's book about an unseen band of singers

explanation.walkthrough: James Lane Allen was an American novelist whose best-known book is The Choir Invisible (1897); the clue reworks its title.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers is a choir, and Allen's novel calls its singers invisible.

clue.text: Bird feeling the cold ?

explanation.surface: A bird shivering in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterer is an old name for birds such as the waxwing; someone feeling the cold has teeth that rattle together.

clue.text: Frequently mollify with decapitation

indicators.note: decapitation cuts off the head, so the first letter of the word for mollify goes

parts.note: to mollify is to soften someone

explanation.surface: Calming someone down regularly by beheading them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something happening many times.

clue.text: Drink with a strange Judy's husband

parts.note: rum is an old informal word for strange or odd
in the Punch and Judy puppet show, Punch is Judy's husband

explanation.surface: Having a drink with an odd puppet husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum punch is a mixed drink of rum, fruit juice and spice.

clue.text: Journalistic employment ?

parts.note: reads as working for a newspaper, the paper being a journal

explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense is office forms and documents; the clue pretends it means a job on a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Office documents and form-filling are the everyday sense; working on a newspaper is the punning sense.

clue.text: The Irishman's form of butter

explanation.surface: Butter as made by an Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman, so the Irishman's is Pat's; small shaped portions of butter are pats.

clue.text: Allowing much freedom by letter

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: Granting liberty in a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A lax, tolerant attitude lets people do as they like.

clue.text: One eventuality for which people marry

definitions.text: One eventuality for which people marry

parts.words: One eventuality for which people marry
parts.note: recalls the wedding vow promising to stay together in good fortune or bad

explanation.walkthrough: The marriage service has the couple take each other 'for better, for worse, for richer, for poorer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The vow names wealthier circumstances as one condition the couple commit to.

clue.text: Players keeping an eye on the score

definitions.text: Players keeping an eye on the score

parts.words: Players keeping an eye on the score
parts.note: sounds like sports players watching the points, but means musicians reading their written music

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a game; here it is the printed music.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of musicians follows the written music as it plays.

clue.text: Bottoms up, that's sleek!

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A toast to a slick finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The keel is the bottom timber of a ship's hull.

clue.text: For climbers to record a change in time? On the contrary

indicators.note: the clue says a change goes into time
reverses the stated relation, so time goes into the word for change instead

parts.note: to alter is to change
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mountaineers want a device to log the time change.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'a change in time' puts the change inside the time; 'On the contrary' swaps that round, so the time goes inside the change.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument measuring height is something climbers use to log how high they are.

clue.text: Hidden reserve of money, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be pronounced, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A secret stash of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A store kept out of sight is a stash or hoard.

clue.text: "The iron — of midnight hath told twelve" (M N Dream)

definitions.text: "The iron — of midnight hath told twelve" (M N Dream)

parts.words: "The iron — of midnight hath told twelve" (M N Dream)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Theseus's speech in A Midsummer Night's Dream, the missing word being the clapper of a bell

explanation.walkthrough: Theseus says this in Act 5 of A Midsummer Night's Dream: the bell's metal clapper has struck twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: The clapper inside a bell is called by the same word as the organ in the mouth.

clue.text: Picture that's recognizable-of a loch ?

explanation.surface: A portrait of a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as 'like Ness', resembling Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait resembling its subject is a good resemblance; a thing like Loch Ness is, split in two, 'like Ness'.

clue.text: Feller to, lift the junk ?

parts.note: lumber is old unwanted furniture, junk
to jack is to lift with a jack

explanation.surface: A man raising the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like 'fellow' but means one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodsman cuts down trees, so he fells them.

clue.text: Plates laid on here for part of a snatched meal?

definitions.text: Plates laid on here for part of a snatched meal?

parts.words: Plates laid on here for part of a snatched meal
parts.note: sounds like dishes set for a hurried dinner course, but plates are racing trophies run for at a track

explanation.walkthrough: A plate is a prize race; read in halves, the answer is a race plus a course, as of a meal eaten in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing grounds stage the races called plates.

clue.text: It's a change from this office job 'to help with the ricks

indicators.note: says that rearranging the answer gives the following words, so those words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A farm hand's office post that helps with haystacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs from the answer to HELP RICKS; reversed, HELP and RICKS rearrange to the answer. Ricks are haystacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The post of a clerk is a desk job in an office.

clue.text: Pink cricketers in retreat

indicators.note: retreating goes backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: bats are batsmen in cricket

explanation.surface: A rosy cricket team withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pink is to pierce lightly with a sword, to wound with a thrust.

clue.text: Trinculo found Caliban a strange one

definitions.text: Trinculo found Caliban a strange one

parts.words: Trinculo found Caliban a strange one
parts.note: alludes to Trinculo sheltering under Caliban's cloak in The Tempest and remarking on misery's strange companions

explanation.walkthrough: In The Tempest Trinculo crawls under Caliban's cloak, saying 'Misery acquaints a man with strange bedfellows'.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion sharing one's sleeping place, here under the same cloak.

clue.text: Poor Webb bidding farewell to the mining town

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is badly made, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: Someone named Webb, unfortunate, saying goodbye to a coal town.
explanation.walkthrough: EBBW VALE is a former coal and steel town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the South Wales valleys that grew up around coal pits.

clue.text: Bird doesn't hear properly -its head in the sand ?

indicators.note: with 'doesn't', saying the word is not heard right, so its letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A deaf bird hiding its head in sand like an ostrich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't hear properly' signals the anagram; 'its head in the sand' is colour from the ostrich legend, the rhea being a South American relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: No hanky-panky-here's the company's chairman

explanation.surface: An honest chairman at the head of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the answer literally: the chairman sits above the board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and honest dealing; a chairman ranks over the directors.

clue.text: Pride preceded this plant in 1648

parts.note: recalls Colonel Pride's expulsion of members from Parliament, an event whose name puts the plant straight after Pride

explanation.walkthrough: In 1648 Colonel Thomas Pride expelled members from Parliament, 'Pride's Purge'; split after the apostrophe's S, the event's name is Pride + the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the euphorbia family, known for milky sap.

clue.text: Assist in getting less than one's full share ?

definitions.text: getting less than one's full share

explanation.surface: Helping out while getting short-changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in an activity; to accept only a portion rather than the whole.

clue.text: With which to claw in the rest of the cards

explanation.surface: A tool for scraping in the remaining cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's hooked nail; in card games the undealt stock pile is also called this.

clue.text: How to beat bad sewing

indicators.note: bad stitching is a mess, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A way to punish poor needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinge is an old word meaning to thrash or flog.

clue.text: Savoured the bouquet-like a circus clown ?

explanation.surface: A clown sniffing the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelt the wine's aroma; a clown has a big red false nose, so is well endowed in that part.

clue.text: Frank does little work in French

parts.note: op is the short form of opus, a work
en is French for in

explanation.surface: An honest man does a bit of work in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and plain-speaking, without concealment.

clue.text: His widow a little tipsy on stage ?

definitions.text: His widow a little tipsy on stage ?

parts.words: His widow a little tipsy on stage
parts.note: a slightly drunk widow on stage is a merry one, pointing to the composer of that operetta

explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehar wrote the operetta The Merry Widow; 'merry' means a little tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian composer whose most famous stage work is about a cheerful widow.

clue.text: A friend enclose odd pairs for valuation

indicators.note: the word for friend goes round the following letters

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend surrounds strange couples before assessing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is the anagram signal; the shuffled letters sit inside the friend, after the clue's A.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment of worth, as of property.

clue.text: One of the measures taken to pinch Warbeck?

parts.note: to nip is to pinch
Perkin Warbeck, the pretender to the English throne in Henry VII's time

explanation.surface: Steps taken to grab a pretender.
explanation.definitionFit: An old small liquid quantity, about half a pint or less.

clue.text: "Die, and — a college, or a cat" (Pope)

definitions.text: "Die, and — a college, or a cat" (Pope)

parts.words: "Die, and — a college, or a cat" (Pope)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Alexander Pope's Moral Essays, the missing verb meaning to bequeath funds

explanation.walkthrough: Pope mocks people who leave their fortunes to a college or a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave money to an institution so that it has a lasting income.
